O envio daquela cópia ocorreu mediante solicitação do próprio gabinete, conforme documentação constante do processo administrativo correspondente." Os dados extraídos do celular de Vorcaro haviam sido formalmente solicitados por outros ministros do STF, o que levou Fachin a questionar a PF sobre o material. No sábado, o presidente do STF marcou para o dia 23 a análise pelo plenário da corte da petição sobre a atuação de Mendonça, que se originou de alegações do ministro Alexandre de Moraes de que o colega teria direcionado investigações contra ele e supostamente cometido crime de responsabilidade e abuso de autoridade. As alegações de Moraes foram uma reação à divulgação por Mendonça de trocas de mensagens entre ele e Vorcaro, o que levou a outra petição, essa sobre a conduta de Moraes, e que será analisada na próxima terça-feira. Também no sábado, Fachin negou pedido de Moraes para que a petição sobre ele fosse analisada conjuntamente com o procedimento sobre Mendonça e também assumiu a relatoria do caso, até então nas mãos de Mendonça.

item.title: Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. (back) out Week 1 amid extension talks
item.description: Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. sat out Week 1 with a back injury amid an "impasse" between the fourth-year defensive back and Pittsburgh's front office in contract extension talks.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. sat out Week 1 with a back injury amid an "impasse" between the fourth-year defensive back and Pittsburgh's front office in contract extension talks. Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Porter and the team have not been able to make progress on a long-term contract extension. ESPN reported Sunday that the Steelers are "listening" to offers for Porter. He was listed as questionable this week. Porter said at the end of training camp that he would consider not suiting up if the two sides didn't make some type of progress toward a new deal. Porter requested a trade and informed the team he is open to moving elsewhere, ESPN reported. "I mean, at the end of the day, it's business, and I know what that is and I got my head straight to understand that," Porter said Friday. Since the end of the 2025 regular season, four cornerbacks have signed contracts averaging at least $30 million annually. Porter, the son of former Steelers outside linebacker Joey Porter Sr., was a second-round pick (No. 32 overall) in the 2023 draft. He has three career interceptions in 47 regular-season games. --Field Level Media

item.title: Dino tira sigilo de investigação sobre desvio de emendas parlamentares para Dark Horse
item.description: O ministro Flávio Dino, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), retirou neste domingo o sigilo das investigações que apuram se houve desvio de emendas parlamentares para a realização do filme "Dark Horse", sobre a vida do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, de acordo com decisão divulgada neste domingo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O ministro Flávio Dino, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), retirou neste domingo o sigilo das investigações que apuram se houve desvio de emendas parlamentares para a realização do filme "Dark Horse", sobre a vida do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, de acordo com decisão divulgada neste domingo. O ministro também determinou que a Polícia Civil de São Paulo encaminhe à Polícia Federal todo material coletado nas investigações feitas pela polícia paulista sobre o caso. Na última semana, a Polícia Federal cumpriu mandados de busca e apreensão contra o deputado federal Mario Frias (PL-SP) no âmbito de operação que apura o desvio de emendas para a produção do filme sobre a vida do ex-presidente. A retirada do sigilo dessas investigações vem após, nos últimos dias, o presidente do STF, Edson Fachin, determinar que o ministro André Mendonça, relator do caso Master na corte, retirasse o sigilo de uma série de procedimentos sobre o caso. A retirada do sigilo revelou que, em julho, Mendonça autorizou a abertura de inquérito contra o senador e candidato à Presidência, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), para apurar os crimes de corrupção, lavagem de dinheiro e evasão de divisas em um caso que envolve a troca de mensagens com o banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, do Master, atualmente preso após a liquidação extrajudicial do banco, na qual o parlamentar pede dinheiro para o filme sobre Bolsonaro. Flávio vem alegando que os pedidos a Vorcaro de recursos para o filme sobre o seu pai se referem a uma relação privada e tem negado quaisquer irregularidades.

item.title: Amateur scouting director of White Sox resigns amid reported allegations
item.description: The amateur scouting director of the Chicago White Sox has resigned and is no longer with the team.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The amateur scouting director of the Chicago White Sox has resigned and is no longer with the team. The club announced the departure of Mike Shirley on Saturday night with no further information given. However, The Athletic reported that Shirley was being investigated internally following allegations of verbal harassment, which included comments both racial and sexual in nature. He had been on administrative leave since the White Sox received an anonymous tip about comments allegedly made by Shirley, 56, last month while attending the Area Code Games in Long Beach, Calif. The event draws about 200 high school players who hope to impress the scouts and MLB team employees in the stands. The results of the internal investigation are not known, and general manager Chris Getz has not addressed the situation. According to The Athletic, Shirley previously had been investigated at least once. That was in 2022, when Major League Baseball received a tip from a former team employee who said Shirley treated scouts from "underrepresented groups" differently. Per the report, the investigation did not turn up bias in the way Shirley hired or dealt with people from diverse groups. The team declined to comment about Shirley, and he did not respond to messages from The Athletic. A former minor league outfielder in the Cleveland organization, Shirley started with the White Sox in a part-time role in 2000. Among the players he signed as a scout was Getz in 2005. He was promoted to director of amateur scouting in September 2019. Among the No. 1 picks taken during his tenure, five have made it to the major leagues: LHPs Garrett Crochet (2020), Noah Schultz (2022) and Hagen Smith (2024), as well as shortstops Colson Montgomery (2021) and Jacob Gonzalez (2023). Waiting their turn are shortstops Billy Carlson (2025) and Roch Cholowsky out of UCLA, who was the No. 1 overall pick this year. Gonzalez played 30 games for the White Sox earlier this season, filling in at first base for an injured Munetaka Murakami. With Murakami's return imminent, Gonzalez was traded to the Pittsburgh Pirates along with pitcher Brandon Eisert for pitching prospect Jaden Woods and future considerations. Getz flipped Crochet in a trade to the Boston Red Sox for four prospects, including catcher Kyle Teel, outfielder Braden Montgomery and infielder Chase Meidroth, all of whom have played a role in Chicago's turnaround season. Heading into Sunday's series finale against the St. Louis Cardinals, the White Sox (76-72) hold a 1 1/2-game lead in the American League Central over the Cleveland Guardians. Chicago lost at least 100 games in each of the past three seasons. --Field Level Media

item.title: Los suecos votan en elección que podría sumar a la extrema derecha al Gobierno
item.description: Los suecos votaron el domingo en unas elecciones muy reñidas que podrían llevar por primera vez al gobierno a un partido de extrema derecha, o bien devolver al país al liberalismo por el que se le conoce desde hace tiempo.
item.dc:creator: Johan Ahlander, Tom Little
item.content:encoded: Los suecos votaron el domingo en unas elecciones muy reñidas que podrían llevar por primera vez al gobierno a un partido de extrema derecha, o bien devolver al país al liberalismo por el que se le conoce desde hace tiempo. La oposición de centroizquierda sueca mantenía una ligera ventaja sobre el gobernante bloque de derecha antes de las elecciones parlamentarias del domingo, mostraban varias encuestas de opinión esta semana. Sin embargo, el primer ministro Ulf Kristersson, que ha ido a la zaga en las encuestas de opinión a lo largo de sus cuatro años en el cargo, ha ido recortando distancias en las últimas semanas de campaña, mientras que su rival, Magdalena Andersson, y sus socialdemócratas han perdido terreno. Kristersson, que ha gobernado durante cuatro años con el apoyo de los Demócratas de Suecia, de extrema derecha, desde fuera de su coalición, dijo que los incorporará formalmente al Gobierno si su bloque gana, rompiendo así un tabú de larga data. "La condición previa para sacar adelante las cosas es, en realidad, la capacidad de comprometerse, de tener una visión clara pero ser pragmático", afirmó en su ciudad natal, donde votó el domingo. "Si conseguimos los votos de la gente, seguiremos haciéndolo durante los próximos cuatro años". El éxito electoral de los Demócratas de Suecia sería bien recibido por los partidos de extrema derecha en auge en Europa, animados por la victoria del partido antiinmigrante Alternativa para Alemania en unas elecciones regionales celebradas la semana pasada en Alemania. La extrema derecha espera obtener avances en las próximas elecciones en toda Europa, siendo la candidatura de la Agrupación Nacional a la presidencia de Francia el año que viene el mayor premio potencial hasta la fecha. La centroizquierda dice que Kristersson ha cruzado una línea al invitar a los Demócratas de Suecia a formar parte del Gobierno. "Es una elección muy importante para Suecia: o bien tenemos por primera vez en el Gobierno a un partido de extrema derecha fundado por neonazis, o bien un Gobierno liderado por mí", dijo la candidata Andersson a Reuters mientras votaba junto a su marido el domingo. Los Demócratas de Suecia reconocen que su partido fue fundado en parte por neonazis y supremacistas blancos en la década de 1980, pero afirman que han expulsado a esos extremistas de sus filas y se han disculpado por su pasado. "NO PARECE SUECIA" Al votar el sábado en Rinkeby, cerca de Estocolmo, el líder de larga trayectoria de los Demócratas de Suecia, Jimmie Akesson, dijo que este barrio, donde vive una de las mayores poblaciones sueco-somalíes del país, "no parece Suecia". Suecia fue durante mucho tiempo uno de los países europeos más acogedores para los inmigrantes. Pero desde que Kristersson llegó al poder hace cuatro años, las políticas han cambiado radicalmente. Se ha abolido la residencia permanente para los refugiados, se han endurecido las normas de asistencia social y se han intensificado las expulsiones de quienes carecen de derecho a permanecer en el país. "Se centran en los musulmanes. Señalan a los musulmanes y a los inmigrantes. Pero los inmigrantes contribuyen a la sociedad", afirmó Kahin Ahmed, de 57 años, un sociólogo que llegó a Suecia desde Somalia como refugiado. Los Demócratas de Suecia se han comprometido a ir más allá, incluyendo la prohibición de la vestimenta femenina que cubra el rostro si llegan al Gobierno. Akesson dijo a Reuters que ese tipo de vestimenta "refleja valores que, en mi opinión, no tienen cabida en Suecia". Los partidarios del bloque de derecha sueco dicen que una victoria supondría un respaldo a las políticas que han ayudado a frenar la violencia de las bandas y a reducir drásticamente la inmigración. Johanna Tornqvist, de 44 años, analista de mercados que votó a favor de la coalición de derecha, dijo que se habían exagerado los temores en torno a la posibilidad de que los Demócratas de Suecia entraran en el Gobierno. "Lo más importante es mantener a los rojos y verdes fuera del Gobierno", afirmó. Sin embargo, Susanne Cherment, una estudiante de 20 años que votaba por primera vez en un colegio electoral de Nacka, al este de Estocolmo, dijo que le parecía "aterrador" que los jóvenes se sintieran atraídos por la extrema derecha. Las encuestas a pie de urna se publicarán poco después del cierre de los colegios electorales, a las 1800 GMT, y se espera que los datos que den una indicación del resultado estén disponibles alrededor de las 1900 GMT. La derecha ya ha acordado formar un gobierno de cuatro partidos liderado por Kristersson en caso de victoria. El camino de Andersson hacia el poder es más incierto debido a las divisiones entre los partidos de la oposición. Su Partido Socialdemócrata ha ido perdiendo terreno en las encuestas de opinión a pesar del apoyo de celebridades como Benny Andersson, de ABBA —sin parentesco alguno—, quien cambió la letra del estribillo de "Mamma Mia" por "Magdalena" en un mitin en el que actuó esta semana. En última instancia, las elecciones podrían decidirse en función de si un pequeño partido de la coalición de Kristersson, los Liberales, supera el umbral del 4% para obtener escaños.

item.title: Trump says US could stay in Iran and keep oil, like Venezuela deal
item.description: He drew a parallel with the U.S. push to take control of a fifth of Venezuela's reserves.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Conor Humphries
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump suggested on Sunday the United States could stay in Iran and "keep the oil", drawing a parallel with [USN:L6N44P14L TEXT:"a U.S. push"] to take control of a fifth of Venezuela's vast oil reserves. On a trip to Ireland for meetings and to watch golf, he reiterated that he still expected the Iran war to end this year, possibly just after midterm elections due in the United States in November. Speaking at the Irish Open golf championship, Trump added that the price of gasoline would "drop like a rock" once the Iran war ended. Turmoil in the Middle East has roiled oil markets, with oil traders expecting prices to rise again on Monday after an attack on [USN:L6N45500C TEXT:"a Saudi oil pipeline"]. Trump said that he would only make the "right deal" and wouldn't do one that was "no good", adding that Iran was "calling constantly" for peace talks — an assertion that Tehran has dismissed in the past. But the president also introduced another option: stay engaged with Iran. He drew a parallel with the U.S. [USN:L6N44R00F TEXT:"deal in Venezuela"], announced in August. "We'll ultimately get out (of Iran), unless we decide to stay and keep the oil like Venezuela," Trump said, adding that the U.S. revenue from Venezuela has "paid for the war many times."

item.title: Valencia sack CEO and manager Corberan after winless start to season
item.description: Valencia dismissed manager Carlos Corberan and chief executive officer Ron Gourlay on Sunday after a winless start to the season.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Valencia dismissed manager Carlos Corberan and chief executive officer Ron Gourlay on Sunday after a winless start to the season. Gourlay and Corberan were under increasing pressure from the club's fans in recent weeks due to the team's poor form. Valencia have a single point from their opening five matches this season, leaving them bottom of LaLiga. Corberan was appointed in December 2024, and steered the club clear of relegation to a 12th-place finish. Last season Valencia finished in ninth place, but the manager's style of football earned criticism at Mestalla and during Valencia's recent home matches, shouts of 'Corberan leave now' were audible from the crowd. In total, he was in charge for 72 games, winning 28 and losing 26. Gourlay joined the club in May 2025. He had defended Corberan's position on multiple occasions in public. Valencia have also terminated the contracts of four staff members working under Gourlay, as well as Corberan's coaching staff. "This decision reflects the club's intention to begin a new phase for the running of the sporting structure and football operations," said Valencia in a statement. "On an interim basis, VCF Mestalla coach Oscar Sanchez will take charge of the first team." Valencia said their new sporting structure will be announced shortly. Their next fixture is on Tuesday against Deportivo Alaves.

item.title: No luck for Norris as Antonelli becomes Madring's first F1 winner
item.description: Mercedes's Kimi Antonelli won the first Spanish Grand Prix held at Madrid's new circuit to take another huge stride towards the Formula One title after bad luck denied Lando Norris victory for McLaren on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Mercedes's Kimi Antonelli won the first Spanish Grand Prix held at Madrid's new circuit to take another huge stride towards the Formula One title after bad luck denied Lando Norris victory for McLaren on Sunday. The 20-year-old Italian's triumph from starting second on the grid at the Madring was his eighth win of the season and stretched his championship lead over teammate George Russell to 81 points after 14 rounds. Red Bull's four-time champion Max Verstappen was second with reigning champion Norris third. Russell finished fifth. "I think today it's good to win but it doesn't feel as good because I think Lando today deserved the win but overall, we take it," said Antonelli. VIRTUAL SAFETY CAR PROVES DECISIVE Antonelli benefited from a virtual safety car (VSC) on lap 15 falling at just the right time for him to come in for a change of tyres and too late for McLaren's pole-sitter Norris, who was leading and had already gone past the pit entrance seconds earlier. When Norris came in at the next opportunity, on lap 16 of 57, the race had gone green again. The pitstop was slow, due to a problem on the front right of the car, but McLaren and Pirelli said that made little difference and the damage had already been done on a track that lived up to fears it would be impossible to overtake. Norris said there was nothing he could do, with all the top three on the same one-stop strategy. "I felt like we deserved it today but that's racing sometimes," he said. "I feel like I drove a perfect race today, just luck wasn't with me. "It's just incredibly frustrating to lose in a way that has nothing to do with performance." OPENING BATTLE BETWEEN ANTONELLI AND NORRIS Antonelli twice had to give the lead back to Norris on the opening lap after cutting corners and gaining an advantage while trying to pass but the Briton then settled into a rhythm and began to pull away. Verstappen also gained places that he had to hand back to Antonelli and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, despite complaining that the latter had "almost shunted into me" and was out of control. Hamilton then suffered a brake problem that sent him plunging down the order and the seven-time world champion was eventually forced to retire. Norris was more than six seconds clear with everything seemingly under control when Aston Martin's Lance Stroll triggered the VSC by stopping at turn 20. Antonelli, Verstappen and Russell all pitted, saving precious seconds compared to a normal stop. When Norris came in for a switch to hard tyres to take him to the end of the race, he was stationary for seven seconds and returned to the track in fifth place but effectively fourth with Ferrari's new leader Charles Leclerc yet to stop. Leclerc stayed out until lap 48, hoping in vain for another safety car to give him a cheap stop, and then pitted. He ended up fourth. The virtual safety car proved decisive, with the remainder of the afternoon effectively a high-speed procession to the chequered flag without major incident -- despite fears that there could be multiple crashes and red flags as seen in earlier junior races -- or much to get excited about. Antonelli crossed the line 4.3 seconds clear of Verstappen with Norris a further 0.7 behind, pushing hard but with no way past. "Of course we know that Lando got unlucky with that VSC, so for us I think today P2 is an incredible result because you could see how much Lando was catching me," said Verstappen. Liam Lawson, standing in for the injured Isack Hadjar for the third race in a row, was sixth for Red Bull with Franco Colapinto seventh for Renault-owned Alpine and Oscar Piastri eighth in a damaged McLaren. Arvid Lindblad secured precious points for Racing Bulls in their battle for fifth with Alpine and Audi's Nico Hulkenberg the final scorer in 10th. Mercedes now have 503 points to Ferrari's 358 and McLaren's 306. The next race is the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in Baku on September 26.

item.title: Antonelli gana primera carrera de la F1 en Madring tras lenta parada en boxes de Norris
item.description: El piloto italiano Kimi Antonelli dio un gran paso hacia el título de la Fórmula 1 el domingo tras ganar el primer Gran Premio de España celebrado en el nuevo circuito de Madrid, con un poco de suerte de por medio.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: El piloto italiano Kimi Antonelli dio un gran paso hacia el título de la Fórmula 1 el domingo tras ganar el primer Gran Premio de España celebrado en el nuevo circuito de Madrid, con un poco de suerte de por medio. La victoria en Madring del italiano de 20 años, su octava de la temporada, amplió su ventaja en el campeonato a 81 puntos tras 14 carreras. Antonelli se benefició de una oportuna salida del coche de seguridad virtual (VSC) y de una desastrosa parada en boxes de McLaren en la vuelta 16 de 57, lo que privó de una probable victoria a Lando Norris, quien arrancó desde la pole position y lideró la carrera en un inicio, en un circuito en el que adelantar resultaba casi imposible. "Creo que hoy está bien ganar, pero no me sabe tan bien porque creo que Lando se merecía la victoria hoy; pero, en general, nos la quedamos", dijo Antonelli. Max Verstappen, de Red Bull, quedó segundo, y Norris, tercero. Antonelli suma ahora 292 puntos, frente a los 211 de su rival más cercano y compañero de equipo, George Russell, que terminó quinto. "No había nada que pudiera hacer... simplemente la suerte no estuvo de nuestro lado", dijo Norris. "Sentí que hoy nos la merecíamos, pero así son las carreras a veces". "Creo que hoy he hecho una carrera perfecta, pero la suerte no me ha acompañado". BATALLA INICIAL POR LAS POSICIONES Antonelli tuvo que ceder el liderato a Norris en dos ocasiones durante la primera vuelta, tras salirse de la pista y haber obtenido una ventaja en la disputa en las primeras curvas, pero el británico encontró entonces su ritmo y empezó a alejarse. Verstappen también ganó una posición que tuvo que ceder a Lewis Hamilton, de Ferrari, lo que permitió que también lo adelantara Antonelli, pero luego adelantó al británico siete veces campeón del mundo, que sufrió un problema en los frenos y acabó retirándose. Norris tenía una ventaja de más de seis segundos y todo parecía bajo control cuando Lance Stroll, de Aston Martin, activó el coche de seguridad virtual al detenerse en la pista en la vuelta 14. Antonelli, Verstappen y Russell entraron todos a boxes para realizar una parada rápida, pero Norris no pudo hacerlo, ya que había superado el punto de entrada, y para cuando volvió a dar la vuelta, el coche de seguridad virtual ya había terminado. McLaren le llamó a boxes de todos modos en la vuelta 16 para cambiar a neumáticos duros, pero estuvo parado siete segundos y volvió a la pista en quinta posición, aunque en la práctica era cuarto, ya que el nuevo líder, Charles Leclerc —que acabó cuarto con Ferrari—, aún no había hecho su parada. Ese fue el momento decisivo, y el resto de la tarde se convirtió, en la práctica, en una procesión a gran velocidad hasta la bandera a cuadros sin incidentes importantes —a pesar de los temores de que pudiera haber múltiples accidentes y banderas rojas, como se había visto en carreras juveniles anteriores—. Antonelli cruzó la línea de meta con una ventaja de 4,3 segundos sobre Verstappen, con Norris a otros 0,7 segundos por detrás. Liam Lawson fue sexto con Red Bull, Franco Colapinto séptimo con Alpine —propiedad de Renault— y Oscar Piastri, de McLaren, octavo. Arvid Lindblad sumó unos valiosos puntos para Racing Bulls en su lucha por el quinto puesto con Alpine, y Nico Hülkenberg, de Audi, fue el último en puntuar, en décima posición.

item.title: Trump demande à l'Ukraine d'arrêter de s'attaquer au diesel russe
item.description: Donald Trump a appelé dimanche le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky à cesser de prendre pour cible les raffineries russes produisant du diesel, liant la flambée des prix de ce carburant aux États-Unis à la guerre en Ukraine plutôt qu'au conflit au Moyen-Orient qu'il a déclenché.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Donald Trump a appelé dimanche le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky à cesser de prendre pour cible les raffineries russes produisant du diesel, liant la flambée des prix de ce carburant aux États-Unis à la guerre en Ukraine plutôt qu'au conflit au Moyen-Orient qu'il a déclenché. "Monsieur Zelensky doit faire une chose: il doit cesser de détruire les stocks de gazole en Russie", a déclaré Donald Trump aux journalistes lors d'un déplacement en Irlande, où il assiste à un tournoi de golf. "Nous en avons parlé avec Monsieur Zelensky. Il existe de nombreuses autres cibles. Ne visez pas le diesel", a-t-il ajouté. La Russie est l'un des principaux producteurs mondiaux de diesel mais le coût de ce carburant, qui a atteint cette semaine un prix moyen record de plus de 6 dollars par gallon aux États-Unis, a surtout flambé depuis l'envolée des cours du pétrole brut due au conflit avec l'Iran et à la fermeture de fait du détroit d'Ormuz, auquel Donald Trump ne parvient pas à trouver une issue. Sur la défensive sur ce sujet qui contredit une de ses promesses de campagne, à l'approche des élections de mi-mandat au Congrès début novembre, le président américain a affirmé dimanche que la pénurie de diesel "n'est pas due au Moyen-Orient, mais à ce qui se passe entre la Russie et l'Ukraine". La Russie a revu à la baisse ses prévisions de production pétrolière pour cette année, les ramenant à leur plus bas niveau depuis 17 ans, et a révisé ses perspectives d'exportation de carburant pour 2026 et 2027 en raison de la guerre, selon un document gouvernemental consulté par Reuters. Donald Trump a par ailleurs répété dimanche que la guerre au Moyen-Orient devrait selon lui prendre fin juste avant ou juste après les élections de mi-mandat, bien que les négociations soient pour le moment au point mort. "Les Iraniens veulent à tout prix parvenir à un accord", a une nouvelle fois soutenu le président américain.

item.title: Al menos 129 personas están desaparecidas tras naufragio de un buque de pasajeros en Indonesia
item.description: Al menos seis personas han fallecido y otras 129 están desaparecidas tras el naufragio en la madrugada del domingo de un buque de pasajeros indonesio en el mar de Java debido al mal tiempo, informó la agencia de búsqueda y rescate.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Al menos seis personas han fallecido y otras 129 están desaparecidas tras el naufragio en la madrugada del domingo de un buque de pasajeros indonesio en el mar de Java debido al mal tiempo, informó la agencia de búsqueda y rescate. Los equipos de rescate lograron salvar a 108 personas del buque "Virgo Transport 8" y seguían buscando a otros supervivientes, añadió la agencia. En un centro de rescate, el pasajero Rinto Arahab contó que se agarró a las barandillas del barco después de que este volcó y que luego logró trepar a un punto más elevado de la embarcación siniestrada mientras esta se balanceaba y daba vueltas en el agua. "Me sentí resignado", dijo a Reuters en la ciudad de Banjarmasin, en Kalimantan del Sur, hacia donde se dirigía el barco antes de perder contacto con las autoridades. "Solo podía rezar por mi seguridad". Los familiares de los pasajeros también se reunieron en la ciudad, a la espera de noticias. Una mujer, que se identificó como Putri, explicó que había estado hablando por teléfono con su marido, Herman, que se encontraba en el barco, antes de que se cortara la comunicación. "Después de eso, ya no hubo más contacto, no pudimos localizarlo", explicó. El barco zarpó el sábado de la ciudad de Surabaya, en Java Oriental, con 243 personas a bordo, incluidos 30 tripulantes, informó la agencia de búsqueda y rescate. Un helicóptero que pasaba por la zona informó que el barco había volcado, dijo el ministro de Transporte, Dudy Purwagandhi, en una rueda de prensa. Añadió que aún se estaba investigando la causa. La agencia de búsqueda y rescate había afirmado anteriormente que el barco se había hundido. Los pasajeros rescatados habían sido trasladados a otros barcos y algunos de ellos serían llevados a un puerto de Java Oriental, dijo en un video I Putu Sudayana, jefe de la oficina de la agencia en Banjarmasin. Indonesia, un archipiélago de 17.000 islas, depende en gran medida de los transbordadores para el transporte, ya que las rutas marítimas son más asequibles y accesibles que los viajes en avión.

item.title: Nick Pivetta, streaking Padres eager to take down Giants
item.description: The San Diego Padres hope right-hander Nick Pivetta can give their overworked bullpen a bit of a break when the team goes for a series sweep of the host San Francisco Giants on Sunday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The San Diego Padres hope right-hander Nick Pivetta can give their overworked bullpen a bit of a break when the team goes for a series sweep of the host San Francisco Giants on Sunday night. Bradgley Rodriguez, Adrian Morejon and Mason Miller have been summoned from the Padres' bullpen in high-leverage situations in the first two games of the series. Miller closed 7-5 and 7-6 wins for San Diego on Friday and Saturday, respectively. The narrow victories have allowed the Padres (80-68) to extend their winning streak to six games and keep the Arizona Diamondbacks (79-70) at arm's length as the teams duel for the third and final wild-card spot in the National League. While Miller has gotten the saves, Morejon has done the most damage to the Giants' comeback efforts in the first two games of the series. The left-hander struck out two of the three men he faced Friday, including Rafael Devers, while protecting a two-run lead, before striking out Devers and Bryce Eldridge in a 1-2-3 eighth inning with San Diego up just 7-6 on Saturday. "He's a dynamic reliever," Padres manager Craig Stammen said of Morejon recently. "He can pitch multiple innings or be dominant for one inning." Pivetta (2-2, 3.43 ERA) is unlikely to take the entire burden off the San Diego bullpen, having only this week returned from nearly a five-month absence due to a strained right elbow. He threw five shutout innings in a 3-2 home win over the Washington Nationals on Monday. Before the injury, the 33-year-old was brilliant in a home start against the Giants on April 1. He limited the visitors to one hit in five innings in a 7-1 win, improving his career record against San Francisco to 5-1 with a 3.83 ERA in 10 games (seven starts). The Giants (62-87) have been fighting an uphill battle almost from the get-go in the first two games of the series. They trailed 7-1 after 4 1/2 innings on Friday, then 7-3 going to the bottom of the eighth in the rematch. San Francisco has five home runs in the series, including two (one a grand slam) by Devers. Shay Whitcomb, Drew Gilbert and Drew Cavanaugh have accounted for the others. Whitcomb, a 27-year-old who played previously for the Houston Astros, wasn't including himself when he told reporters this week that "the young guys just bring a lot of energy. "You've seen that even in our losses the last couple weeks," he continued. "We've been fighting until the very end. It's been really fun to have such a hungry group." In the series finale, that group will support right-hander Logan Webb (8-8, 4.10 ERA), who rebounded from a rough three-game stretch to throw six one-run innings in his team's 5-4 home win in 11 innings over the St. Louis Cardinals on Monday. Webb, 29, will face the Padres for the third time this season, having split decisions in the two earlier matchups, allowing nine runs in 10 innings. He has gone 5-6 with a 3.60 ERA in 19 career appearances (18 starts) vs. San Diego. --Field Level Media

item.title: D-backs' Eduardo Rodriguez aims to continue as stopper vs. Rangers
item.description: Five of Arizona left-hander Eduardo Rodriguez's 15 wins have come after a team loss, and the Diamondbacks could use him now more than ever.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Five of Arizona left-hander Eduardo Rodriguez's 15 wins have come after a team loss, and the Diamondbacks could use him now more than ever. "He's a stopper," Arizona manager Torey Lovullo said. "You know, every fifth day you get a really, really good chance at winning a baseball game. That's nice to know." Rodriguez (15-5, 2.55 ERA) will oppose solid Texas right-hander Cal Quantrill (8-5, 2.89) in the finale of a three-game series in Phoenix that has playoff implications for both. The Rangers (73-76) gained a game in both the American League West and wild-card races with their 6-2 win Saturday. They are two games behind Houston (75-74) in the division and two behind Cleveland (75-74) for the third AL wild-card spot. The D-backs (79-70) are 1 1/2-games behind San Diego (80-68) for the third NL wild card. The Chicago Cubs (83-66) are one game ahead of Philadelphia (82-67) for the top spot. Texas added reinforcements for the stretch drive Saturday, and both right-hander Nathan Eovaldi and third baseman Josh Jung made immediate contributions. Eovaldi pitched 2 2/3 innings of relief in his first regular-season appearance out of the bullpen since 2019, and Jung had two hits and an RBI. Both were activated from the injured list before the game. "'Evo' had 45 pitches tonight and I was going to use every one of them," Texas manager Skip Schumaker said. "I thought he got better as he was going. I wanted to keep going (with him), but his health is always in the back of my mind. "Now that J.J. (Jung) is back, I'm going to give him some runway. He's earned it. This is not about feelings or anything. We don't have time. We've got to go." Rodriguez is tied for second in the NL wins and third in ERA, which would be the best of his career after he posted a 3.30 ERA with Detroit before signing a four-year $80 million free agent deal with the D-backs. He is 5-1 with a 1.96 ERA in his last six outings, four quality starts. "He fills the strike zone," Lovullo said. "He gets big outs. He doesn't get too excited. He never gets rattled or jangled." Rodriguez is 4-1 with a 5.08 ERA in seven career starts against the Rangers, although he has not faced them since 2022. Jake Burger is 3-for-8 against him. Corey Seager is 2-for-9. Quantrill has hit his stride after opening the season in the bullpen. He is 4-1 with a 1.69 ERA with quality starts in his last five appearances and was the Rangers' pitcher of the month for August while taking over after injuries to Eovaldi and Jack Leiter. "He's pitched like an ace," Schumaker said. "I don't know what we'd be doing (without him), because he's not only provided quality start after quality start but he's become this innings eater as well, which has been huge. "Cal has been that guy that stops the bleeding and has provided that for us. He's been excellent." Quantrill beat Seattle 10-5 his last time out Tuesday, giving up three runs in six innings after throwing seven shutout innings in a 6-0 win over Tampa Bay on Sept. 3. He is 2-3 with a 5.68 ERA in nine appearances, seven starts, against the D-backs. He got the win in a 6-5 walkoff victory with an inning of scoreless relief May 13. Ketel Marte is 4 for 14 with two homers against him. -Field Level Media

item.title: Trump tells Ukraine's Zelenskiy to stop hitting Russian diesel
item.description: Long-distance Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian oil refineries in recent months have reduced that country's fuel production, triggering gasoline shortages across the country.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson
item.content:encoded: U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday called on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy to stop targeting Russian diesel infrastructure, saying the attacks were causing a shortage of the fuel that is "hurting the world". A wave of long-distance Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian oil refineries in recent months has reduced that country's fuel production, triggering gasoline shortages across the country. Ukraine, which faces regular Russian attacks on its own energy infrastructure, says refineries are legitimate military targets. The U.S. national average price for diesel, which is used by trucks, trains, ships and farm equipment, [USN:L6N4521A4 TEXT:"rose over $6"] a gallon for the first time on Thursday, according to price tracker GasBuddy. "Mr. Zelenskiy has to do one thing: He has to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia," Trump told journalists during a visit to the Irish Open, which is being held in the west of Ireland on a golf course owned by his family. "We spoke to Mr. Zelenskiy about it. There are plenty of other targets. Don't hit diesel fuel. That's hurting the world," he said. The global shortage "isn't done by the Middle East, this is done by what's happening with Russia and Ukraine," Trump added. Russia [USN:L8N44P12J TEXT:"downgraded"] its oil output forecast for this year to a 17-year low and revised its fuel exports outlook for 2026 and 2027 due to the war, according to a government draft forecast seen by Reuters.

item.title: Trump says 'very negative forces' raising exaggerated concerns over AI
item.description: The public debate heated up after two Anthropic researchers warned that the technology could lead to the extinction of the human race in the not-too-distant future.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Padraic Halpin
item.content:encoded: U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday likened critics of artificial intelligence to "very negative forces" bringing up scenarios that will not happen, and said he wanted to make sure that the U.S. remains the industry leader. "We're leading China in AI. We're the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI wins," Trump told reporters at his Ireland golf course, when asked if the AI industry should slow down or be more regulated. "We could put guardrails. We can do this and that. But I think you have a lot of very negative forces that are bringing it up that shouldn't be bringing it up and they're bringing up things that won't happen." Trump has resisted stirring concerns about AI. The public debate about AI has heated up in the U.S. after two Anthropic researchers [USN:L6N4520JA TEXT:"issued warnings"] that the rapidly progressing technology could lead to the extinction of the human race in the not-too-distant future. In his second term, Trump's administration has largely embraced AI firms. These AI leaders and other technology companies have also supported Trump's initiatives. AI executives have [USN:L6N44212E TEXT:"poured money"] into the midterm campaign ahead of the November 3 election that will determine control of Congress. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk's super PAC, America PAC, has already [USN:L6N4520O8 TEXT:"spent millions"] backing Republican candidates and is expected to play a major role in voter turnout efforts this fall. The Pentagon this year [USN:L6N3ZZ12R TEXT:"warned of risks"] from Anthropic's model. After the researcher warnings, some AI CEOs are pushing for slowing advancement of the models. On Saturday, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei outlined a [USN:L1N45403P TEXT:"three-step framework"] intended to pace development and create more time to manage its risks.The proposal immediately received endorsements from several other executives at major AI companies, including Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. In an interview that aired Sunday on the CBS program "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," Amodei said the competition between U.S. and Chinese AI companies was the "toughest dilemma" in trying to establish a "speed limit" on the rate of AI development. "We shouldn't kid ourselves, because the incentives to pull ahead and the military advantage that you get from that are so large that the ability to check that the other side isn't cheating has to be ironclad," he said. "So I think that's going to be the work of years, and honestly, I don't know if it's possible." Jacob Coxon, one of the Anthropic researchers who resigned and then issued the warnings, pushed for the U.S. to work with other countries to ensure pace. "I feel we need international coordination, or else we risk running the same race with China, which could be equally dangerous," Coxon said on NBC's Meet the Press.

item.title: Ronaldo calls for lifetime bans after 'Jota' chants aimed at Neves
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo said on Sunday that fans who appeared to make chants referencing former teammate Diogo Jota at Ruben Neves during a Saudi Pro League match should be banned from football stadiums for life.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cristiano Ronaldo said on Sunday that fans who appeared to make chants referencing former teammate Diogo Jota at Ruben Neves during a Saudi Pro League match should be banned from football stadiums for life. The chants occurred on Saturday during a fixture between Al-Taawoun and Neves' side Al-Hilal in Buraidah, Saudi Arabia. [USN:S8N3QE0AD TEXT:"Jota died on July 3, 2025"], in a car crash in Zamora, northwestern Spain, along with his brother Andre Silva. A close friend of Jota, [USN:L4N3T2013 TEXT:"Neves was a pallbearer"] at his funeral. Footage filmed from the stands during the match and circulated on social media appeared to show supporters chanting 'Jota'. The shouts attracted the attention of Neves, who pointed to his eye and then up to the sky in response. Passing through the mixed zone after the game, Neves commented, "I hope they don't go to pray afterwards." In response to an Instagram post showing the footage, Ronaldo commented from his personal account. "The league must take action and punish this kind of fan behaviour," said Ronaldo. "This is no longer football, and there have to be limits. People who behave like this should never be allowed to enter a stadium again." The game finished 6-0 to Al-Hilal, with Neves playing 75 minutes before being substituted. Al-Hilal Club Company announced in a statement on their website on Sunday that they had filed a complaint with the Saudi Arabian Football Federation relating to the incident. The Saudi Pro League club were "confident" that measures would be taken to "protect the integrity of sporting competition from offensive practices." "The Company expressed its absolute rejection of such actions targeting players or their families, or intended to cause personal offence," said Al-Hilal's statement. Later on Sunday, Al-Taawoun also released a statement regarding the incident, which strongly condemned the offensive chants. "Such conduct is completely unacceptable and does not represent Al-Taawoun, its supporters or the values for which its terraces are known." Al-Taawoun say they will "take all necessary measures in coordination with the relevant authorities to prevent a recurrence and hold offenders accountable."

item.title: France apologises for human rights criticism that sparked US walkout
item.description: France's mission to the United Nations in Geneva has said it "regrets" criticising the United States over human rights in a social media post that triggered a diplomatic dispute which has delayed the arrival of a new French ambassador in Washington.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: France's mission to the United Nations in Geneva has said it "regrets" criticising the United States over human rights in a social media post that triggered a diplomatic dispute which has delayed the arrival of a new French ambassador in Washington. In a post on X in late July, the French mission had criticised the United States for joining countries including Russia and North Korea in voting against extending the term of U.N. human rights chief Volker Turk. The message [USN:L6N43T12U TEXT:"angered Washington"], which responded by walking out of a U.N. Security Council meeting while France was speaking. Sources said the U.S. was also weighing [USN:L1N43V0F5 TEXT:"blocking France's choice"] as its next ambassador in Washington. "The Permanent Mission of France to the U.N. in Geneva regrets the 25 July 2026 message posted on X that called into question the U.S. commitment to human rights," the mission said. The difference in views "concerned one vote, and not the defence of human rights," it said in a statement in English published on its website. France's foreign affairs ministry declined to comment further. “We note and appreciate France’s statement, and look forward to working together to further shared values and interests,” a State Department official said in response to a Reuters request for comment. The apology, earlier reported by French daily Le Monde, may open the way for France's nominee as next ambassador to the U.S., Aurelien Lechevallier, to be approved by Washington. Lechevallier, a former Elysee aide, is currently Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot's chief of staff. Paris had aimed to have him in post by September, a source has said.

item.title: League-leading Rays strive for sweep of Astros
item.description: After clinching a spot in the playoffs, the Tampa Bay Rays were not interested in taking Saturday night off.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: After clinching a spot in the playoffs, the Tampa Bay Rays were not interested in taking Saturday night off. The American League's top team stretched its lead in the East Division to four games in a 3-2 win over Houston and will try to sweep the Astros on Sunday afternoon in St. Petersburg, Fla. So far, it's been a weekend to remember for the Rays (89-59), who have started their nine-game homestand with two slim victories over the AL West-leading Astros (75-74). It was Junior Caminero's heroics with a walk-off homer Friday, but reliever Bryan Baker crafted his second save of at least four outs this season to end any chance Houston had of squaring the series and gaining ground on the second-place Texas Rangers. "I definitely didn't expect it," replied Baker, who notched his majors-high 40th save, when told he had converted 29 in a row. "When you're a part of such a good team and you get in those situations, a lot of good things can happen. It's a team stat." Houston's scheduled starter on Sunday, Hayden Wesneski (5-1, 3.35 ERA), has had only eight starts in 2026, but the Houston native has been on a roll since returning from Tommy John surgery. The 28-year-old right-hander has been reliable in a rotation that desperately needed stability, and the most important thing he has supplied is quality innings deeper into games. That ability became more important at the trade deadline last month when the Astros' rotation was weakened after the team dealt Spencer Arrighetti to the Toronto Blue Jays for Gold Glove outfielder Daulton Varsho, then did not add another pitcher. The Astros pitcher has won three of his past four starts, going 3-0 with a 1.57 ERA and perhaps throwing his best game two starts ago against the Chicago White Sox but getting no decision. Over seven shutout innings, he allowed just a third-inning single to Tristan Peters and only five base-runners overall as Houston won 2-0 at home on Sept. 2. "We have a really good analytics side," said Wesneski, whose squad is 7-1 in his starts. "They help us out with the pitching and the preparation. ... Being prepared really does put you in a good spot going out there." Wesneski has no record and a 1.69 ERA in two relief outings against the Rays, who appear to have found the version of Freddy Peralta they were hoping to have traded for. Following the right-hander's first two starts with his new club after the trade deadline -- terrible outings that more closely resembled his half-season with the New York Mets -- the Rays have worked with Peralta (8-11, 4.82 ERA) and brought about good results heading into his start on Sunday. In those first two starts at the Colorado Rockies and Athletics, Peralta surrendered 10 runs in 9 2/3 innings, but he has turned it around in the past three outings and looks like the pitcher nicknamed "Fastball Freddy." The 30-year-old has tossed 18 innings and allowed just two runs and 10 hits while fanning 13, with just one walk, in those three outings. His 3-0 record and 1.00 ERA in that span show he is pointed in the right direction. Added manager Kevin Cash: "The last three (starts) for us is probably a closer version to the guy he's been his entire career." In two starts and a relief outing against Houston, Peralta is 0-2 with a 10.24 ERA. --Field Level Media

item.title: Cubs aim to keep wild-card pace, sweep fading Pirates
item.description: The Cubs' bullpen delivered a much-needed steady performance while the Pittsburgh Pirates are running out of time in the National League wild-card race entering Sunday's series finale in Chicago.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Cubs' bullpen delivered a much-needed steady performance while the Pittsburgh Pirates are running out of time in the National League wild-card race entering Sunday's series finale in Chicago. Chicago (83-66) holds a one-game lead over the Philadelphia Phillies for the NL's top wild-card spot. The Pirates (74-75) are 6 1/2 games behind the San Diego Padres for the third and final wild-card spot. Pittsburgh let a 3-2 lead in the eighth-inning slip away on Saturday. The Cubs scored twice in the inning despite collecting just one hit as Pirates reliever Gregory Soto issued two walks and hit two batters in Chicago's 4-3 victory. Pirates manager Don Kelly knew his club let an important one get away. "There's no doubt that one hurts," Kelly said. "We have to find a way. We've done it this season. We have to show up with that same mindset and go out and attack." While the Cubs' relievers have struggled lately, they combined for 3 1/3 scoreless innings on Saturday, allowing one hit and one walk while striking out two. Ryan Rolison threw 1 2/3 innings of scoreless relief and said results are all that matter as the season hits the stretch run. "This time of year it's a full team effort," Rolison said. "Whatever you can do to get outs, whatever it takes, it takes a full team effort." In 54 appearances, Rolison has gone 9-1 with two saves, seven holds and a 2.76 ERA. Cubs manager Craig Counsell praised the effort the left-hander has given. "Ryan has pitched really well," Counsell said. "Better than the line has shown lately and we are going to need to count on him for big outs." Even though the Chicago bullpen wasn't needed in Friday's 12-2 blowout, Counsell knows it's all about weathering the storm as a reliever. "Being a high leverage reliever sometimes you get beat and it hurts but you get the next night and say go do it again," Counsell said. Pittsburgh turns to rookie right-hander Bubba Chandler (7-9, 4.25 ERA) to avoid the sweep. His two career starts against the Cubs have come this season, and he is 0-0 with a 6.10 ERA over 10 1/3 innings. In his last start, he lifted the Pirates to a 9-3 road victory over the Chicago White Sox, allowing two runs on four hits with no walks and eight strikeouts over six innings. Chandler, 23, has developed a rapport with a fellow rookie, catcher Rafael Flores Jr., 25. "Each start is a growing moment for me," Chandler said. "It's also a growing moment for him. He's a great catcher now and is going to get even better." Chicago is set to counter with left-hander Matthew Boyd (8-4, 4.03). In nine career starts against the Pirates, Boyd is 1-3 with a 5.44 ERA. He's posted 46 strikeouts and 17 walks in 46 1/3 innings. Boyd took the loss in his last start on Monday, a 4-3 setback at the Milwaukee Brewers, allowing three runs on five hits with two walks and seven strikeouts over seven innings. -Field Level Media

item.title: Nepal tunnel survivor finds solace in village homecoming
item.description: After nine days trapped in a hydropower tunnel and a week of hospital care following his dramatic rescue, Sanjay Sah, a rare survivor of last month's devastating glacier collapse in Nepal, finally returned to his village and family on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Sahana Bajracharya
item.content:encoded: After nine days trapped in a hydropower tunnel and a week of hospital care following his [USN:L4N45317T TEXT:"dramatic rescue"], Sanjay Sah, a rare survivor of last month's devastating glacier collapse in Nepal, finally returned to his village and family on Sunday. It was a homecoming marked by relief and joy but also grief. "I was trapped in the tunnel ... I felt trapped in the hospital room too. I finally feel free here in my village," Sah, 30, said after arriving in Tilathi Koiladi, near the border with India. At least 1,386 people have died and 5,130 are still missing across Nepal weeks after a Himalayan glacier collapsed near the Chinese border, unleashing a wall of mud and water that crashed through mountain valleys destroying everything in its path. Around 900 power station workers remain missing. Sah, a mechanical foreman at the Upper Trishuli 3A Hydropower Station, was one of just three [USN:L6N44W0G4 TEXT:"pulled from debris-buried tunnels"] extending deep under the mountains. He survived in the darkness, drinking flood water and seepage from the mountain rock until rescue workers finally reached him. Sah left the hospital in the capital Kathmandu on Friday and the next day boarded a bus for an overnight journey home. A TEARFUL HOMECOMING TO A VILLAGE STILL IN MOURNING Around 60 people, mostly women, awaited his arrival in Tilathi Koiladi on Sunday. Family members, including his parents, uncle, wife and daughter, performed a traditional welcome ceremony, washing his feet as part of a cleansing ritual. After his mother dabbed a pink vermilion tika on his forehead, Sah bowed. They embraced and then broke down in tears. "My son!" his mother cried, holding him tightly and kissing him on the cheek. Women who had gathered to witness the reunion used their colourful saris to wipe the tears from their eyes. Many in Tilathi Koiladi are still awaiting word of the fate of family members who had been working at hydropower stations hit by the flooding. "There are more people from my village still missing after the flood," Sah told Reuters. One family, he said, phoned him while he was still in the hospital to ask if he had seen or heard from a missing relative who had been working at a different power station. He had to tell them he had not. At home among family, Sah said he is ready to put his ordeal behind him. "I will stay in my village for some time now. I want to meet all my people," he said. "But if I am called back to duty, I will go."

item.title: Trump dice que EEUU podría permanecer en Irán y quedarse con el petróleo, como en acuerdo con Venezuela
item.description: El presidente Donald Trump sugirió el domingo que Estados Unidos podría permanecer en Irán y "quedarse con el petróleo", estableciendo un paralelismo con la iniciativa estadounidense de hacerse con el control de una quinta parte de las enormes reservas petroleras de Venezuela.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Conor Humphries
item.content:encoded: El presidente Donald Trump sugirió el domingo que Estados Unidos podría permanecer en Irán y "quedarse con el petróleo", estableciendo un paralelismo con la iniciativa estadounidense de hacerse con el control de una quinta parte de las enormes reservas petroleras de Venezuela. Durante un viaje a Irlanda para asistir a reuniones y ver un torneo de golf, reiteró que seguía esperando que la guerra con Irán termine este año, posiblemente justo después de las elecciones legislativas de mitad de mandato que se celebrarán en Estados Unidos en noviembre. En declaraciones realizadas durante el campeonato de golf Irish Open, Trump añadió que el precio de la gasolina "caería en picado" una vez que termine la guerra con Irán. La agitación en Oriente Medio ha sacudido los mercados petroleros, y los operadores de crudo prevén que los precios vuelvan a subir el lunes tras un ataque contra un oleoducto saudí. Trump dijo que solo aceptaría el "acuerdo adecuado" y que no firmaría uno que "no valiera la pena", añadiendo que Irán estaba "pidiendo constantemente" negociaciones de paz —una afirmación que Teherán ha desmentido en el pasado—. Pero el presidente también planteó otra opción: seguir manteniendo el diálogo con Irán. Estableció un paralelismo con el acuerdo de Estados Unidos en Venezuela, anunciado en agosto. "Al final nos retiraremos (de Irán), a menos que decidamos quedarnos y quedarnos con el petróleo, como en Venezuela", dijo Trump, añadiendo que los ingresos de Estados Unidos procedentes de Venezuela han "pagado la guerra muchas veces".

item.title: Trump le dice al presidente ucraniano Zelenski que deje de atacar el diésel ruso
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, pidió el domingo al presidente ucraniano, Volodímir Zelenski, que deje de atacar la infraestructura de diésel rusa, alegando que los ataques estaban provocando una escasez del combustible que "está perjudicando al mundo".
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, pidió el domingo al presidente ucraniano, Volodímir Zelenski, que deje de atacar la infraestructura de diésel rusa, alegando que los ataques estaban provocando una escasez del combustible que "está perjudicando al mundo". Una oleada de ataques con drones ucranianos a larga distancia contra refinerías de petróleo rusas en los últimos meses ha reducido la producción de combustible de ese país, lo que ha provocado una escasez de gasolina en todo el territorio. Ucrania, que se enfrenta a ataques rusos constantes contra su propia infraestructura energética, dice que las refinerías son objetivos militares legítimos. El precio promedio nacional del diésel en Estados Unidos, que utilizan camiones, trenes, barcos y maquinaria agrícola, superó el jueves por primera vez los 6 dólares por galón, según el comparador de precios GasBuddy. "El señor Zelenski tiene que hacer una cosa: tiene que dejar de atacar el suministro de diésel en Rusia", dijo Trump a periodistas durante una visita al Abierto de Irlanda, que se celebra en el oeste de Irlanda en un campo de golf propiedad de su familia. "Hablamos con el señor Zelenski sobre ello. Hay muchos otros objetivos. Que no ataque el diésel. Eso está perjudicando al mundo", afirmó. La escasez mundial "no se debe a Oriente Medio, sino a lo que está ocurriendo con Rusia y Ucrania", añadió Trump. Rusia ha rebajado su previsión de producción de petróleo para este año a su nivel más bajo en 17 años y ha revisado sus perspectivas de exportación de combustible para 2026 y 2027 debido a la guerra, según un borrador de previsiones del Gobierno al que ha tenido acceso Reuters.

item.title: Trump dice que "fuerzas muy negativas" están generando preocupaciones exageradas sobre la IA
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, comparó el domingo a los detractores de la inteligencia artificial con "fuerzas muy negativas" que plantean escenarios que no se producirán, y dijo que quería asegurarse de que Estados Unidos siga siendo líder del sector.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Padraic Halpin
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, comparó el domingo a los detractores de la inteligencia artificial con "fuerzas muy negativas" que plantean escenarios que no se producirán, y dijo que quería asegurarse de que Estados Unidos siga siendo líder del sector. "Lideramos a China en IA. Somos el país más avanzado del mundo y, francamente, quiero que siga siendo así, porque quien gane en IA, gana", dijo Trump a periodistas en su campo de golf de Irlanda, cuando se le preguntó si el sector de la IA debería ralentizarse o estar más regulado. "Podríamos establecer medidas de protección. Podemos hacer esto y aquello. Pero creo que hay muchas fuerzas muy negativas que están sacando el tema a colación cuando no deberían hacerlo, y están planteando cosas que no van a suceder". Trump se ha resistido a avivar las preocupaciones sobre la IA. El debate público sobre la IA ha ganado fuerza en Estados Unidos después de que dos investigadores de Anthropic advirtieron que esta tecnología, que avanza a pasos agigantados, podría provocar la extinción de la raza humana en un futuro no muy lejano. En su segundo mandato, el Gobierno de Trump ha dado un gran apoyo a las empresas de IA. Estos líderes del sector de la IA y otras empresas tecnológicas también han respaldado las iniciativas de Trump. Los ejecutivos del sector de la IA han invertido grandes sumas de dinero en la campaña para las elecciones legislativas de mitad de mandato, que se celebrarán el 3 de noviembre y determinarán quién controlará el Congreso. El super PAC de Elon Musk, director ejecutivo de SpaceX, "America PAC", ya ha gastado millones en apoyar a candidatos republicanos y se espera que desempeñe un papel fundamental en los esfuerzos por fomentar la participación electoral este otoño boreal. El Pentágono advirtió este año de los riesgos que plantea el modelo de Anthropic. Tras las advertencias de los investigadores, algunos directores generales del sector de la IA están presionando para que se ralentice el avance de los modelos. El sábado, el director ejecutivo de Anthropic, Dario Amodei, esbozó un marco de tres pasos destinado a moderar el ritmo de desarrollo y disponer de más tiempo para gestionar sus riesgos. La propuesta recibió inmediatamente el respaldo de varios otros ejecutivos de importantes empresas de IA, entre ellos Musk y el director ejecutivo de OpenAI, Sam Altman. En una entrevista emitida el domingo en el programa "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" de CBS, Amodei dijo que la competencia entre las empresas de IA estadounidenses y chinas era el "dilema más difícil" a la hora de intentar establecer un "límite de velocidad" en el ritmo de desarrollo de la IA. "No debemos engañarnos, porque los incentivos para tomar la delantera y la ventaja militar que ello supone son tan grandes que la capacidad de comprobar que la otra parte no está haciendo trampa tiene que ser a toda prueba", afirmó. "Así que creo que eso va a llevar años y, sinceramente, no sé si será posible". Jacob Coxon, uno de los investigadores de Anthropic que renunció y posteriormente lanzó estas advertencias, instó a Estados Unidos a colaborar con otros países para garantizar un ritmo adecuado. "Creo que necesitamos coordinación internacional; de lo contrario, corremos el riesgo de enzarzarnos en la misma carrera con China, lo que podría resultar igualmente peligroso", dijo Coxon en el programa "Meet the Press" de NBC.

item.title: Antes de reunión de la Fed, Trump dice que EEUU debería tener tasa más baja del mundo
item.description: El presidente Donald Trump dijo el domingo que ningún país debería tener tasas de interés más bajas que Estados Unidos, a pocos días de la próxima reunión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Padraic Halpin, Conor Humphries
item.content:encoded: El presidente Donald Trump dijo el domingo que ningún país debería tener tasas de interés más bajas que Estados Unidos, a pocos días de la próxima reunión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal. En declaraciones a periodistas durante el torneo de golf Irish Open, Trump dijo que no sabía si los responsables a cargo de la política monetaria de la Fed subirían las tasas de interés en su reunión de esta semana. No obstante, defendió que Estados Unidos "debería tener la tasa de interés más baja del mundo", independientemente de lo que indiquen los datos de la Reserva Federal sobre la inflación y la economía. La reunión de la Fed tendrá lugar menos de una semana después de que un indicador clave de la inflación subyacente, el Índice de Precios al Consumidor del Departamento de Trabajo, registró el viernes su mayor subida en cuatro meses. Esto reforzó las expectativas de que el banco central estadounidense subirá las tasas. Los gobernadores del banco central se reúnen apenas unas semanas antes de las elecciones legislativas de mitad de mandato, que determinarán si los republicanos conservan sus escasas mayorías en ambas cámaras del Congreso de Estados Unidos. Una subida de las tasas podría agravar las preocupaciones de los votantes sobre la asequibilidad, según recientes encuestas de Reuters/Ipsos. Los índices de aprobación de Trump han caído a medida que la inflación se ha mantenido alta. El republicano ha argumentado que los niveles de las tasas de interés de la Fed han favorecido a otros países a costa de Estados Unidos. "Sé más de fórmulas que nadie y, con el mejor crédito del mundo, hacemos ricos a otros países", dijo Trump el domingo. El presidente, que ha criticado con frecuencia al expresidente de la Fed, Jay Powell, se ha mostrado más favorable al liderazgo de la Fed desde que su propio candidato a la presidencia, Kevin Warsh, asumió el cargo a principios de este año. Sin embargo, Trump ha dejado más claras sus exigencias recientemente. "BAJEN LAS TASAS O DEJARÉ DE COMERCIAR CON LOS PAÍSES CON LOS QUE TENEMOS DÉFICIT", publicó Trump en las redes sociales hace dos semanas. Trump "defenderá la independencia de Kevin Warsh por encima de todo", independientemente de lo que haga la Fed con las tasas de interés, dijo el director del Consejo Económico Nacional, Kevin Hassett, en el programa "Fox News Sunday". No obstante, Hassett también subrayó las preferencias del propio Trump, afirmando que "si se trata de una subida de tasas… estoy seguro de que no le va a hacer mucha gracia".

item.title: Kosovo parliament re-elects Albin Kurti as prime minister, political crisis persists
item.description: Kosovo's parliament re-elected Albin Kurti as prime minister on Sunday after his party came first in June elections, but a failure to elect a president could send the country into another snap election.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kosovo's parliament re-elected Albin Kurti as prime minister on Sunday after his party came first in June elections, but a failure to elect a president could send the country into another snap election. Kurti was elected with 62 votes in the 120-seat parliament. "This mandate is about strongly restoring security and prosperity for citizens," Kurti said before the vote. "Repeated elections have only interrupted the same government from governing." In late August, Kurti reached a deal with the opposition Democratic League of Kosovo (LDK), which has 18 MPs, to back law professor Bekim Sejdiu as the new president. A day later, six LDK lawmakers said they would not respect their leader's decision. It remains unclear when the presidential vote will take place. If parliament fails to elect a new president, Kosovo would have to hold another snap election, the fourth in only two years. Kosovo, one of Europe's poorest countries, aims to join the European Union but Brussels has repeatedly said the country needs stable institutions capable of delivering reforms required for membership. Political instability has delayed reforms and slowed access to EU funding. Two-thirds of votes are needed to elect the president, who largely has a ceremonial role. Two opposition parties, the Democratic Party of Kosovo (PDK) and the Alliance, boycotted the session and said they would ask the Constitutional Court whether the law was violated when parliament was constituted. LDK also did not take part in the voting of the new government.

item.title: Carney défend l'idée de faire du Canada un "membre associé" de l'UE-presse
item.description: Le Premier ministre canadien Mark Carney souhaite resserrer les liens l'Union européenne (UE) et examine la possibilité pour son pays de devenir un "membre associé" du bloc, rapporte dimanche le Wall Street Journal.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le Premier ministre canadien Mark Carney souhaite resserrer les liens l'Union européenne (UE) et examine la possibilité pour son pays de devenir un "membre associé" du bloc, rapporte dimanche le Wall Street Journal. L'UE, qui ne s'est pas montrée très souple par le passé en matière de règles d'adhésion, serait ouverte à l'idée d'accorder au Canada un statut de membre associé qui reste à créer, ajoute le journal, citant des responsables anonymes, tant du côté de l'UE que du Canada. L'ambassade du Canada à Bruxelles et les porte-parole de la Commission européenne n'ont pas répondu à des demandes de commentaires. L'escalade dans la guerre commerciale entre le Canada et les États-Unis a rendu plus urgente encore pour Ottawa la recherche d'autres partenaires. Les relations entre les deux pays se sont nettement dégradées depuis le retour du président Donald Trump à la Maison blanche, début 2025, en raison de désaccords sur le commerce et d'autres sujets. Leur différend commercial a conduit à la mise en place de droits de douane portant sur des dizaines de milliards de dollars d'échanges transfrontaliers. Le Canada et l'UE discutent actuellement des moyens de permettre la libre circulation des biens, des services et des travailleurs canadiens impliqués dans des chaînes d'approvisionnement stratégiques telles que l'énergie, l'intelligence artificielle, la défense et les minéraux critiques, ce qui reviendrait à déplacer de fait la frontière de l'UE, selon le Wall Street Journal. Le Canada et l'UE discutent également de la pose de câbles sous-marins, de la construction conjointe de centres de données, de solutions de stockage dans le cloud ainsi que de nouveaux réseaux satellitaires et d'infrastructures permettant d'acheminer l'énergie canadienne vers l'UE, précise le journal. Mark Carney s'est entretenu régulièrement avec plusieurs dirigeants de l'UE, notamment le président français Emmanuel Macron, au sujet de la possibilité de permettre aux Canadiens de vivre et de travailler sans visa dans l'UE, toujours selon le Wall Street Journal, qui cite deux sources anonymes au fait du dossier. Les deux dirigeants se rencontreront le 20 septembre à Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon à l'occasion d'un déplacement d'Emmanuel Macron dans l'archipel. "Dans un monde marqué par le retour des rapports de force, les tensions géopolitiques et de nouvelles dépendances, la France et le Canada partagent une même ambition : travailler ensemble, et avec tous les pays qui partagent ces valeurs, renforcer leur capacité à décider, et à agir par eux-mêmes", a déclaré l'Elysée. Le projet visant à resserrer les liens entre le Canada et l'UE n'est toutefois pas une mince affaire, comme l'a montré la vive opposition suscitée par un accord commercial pourtant plus modeste noué entre les deux parties. Plus d'une décennie après la conclusion de celui-ci et neuf ans après son entrée en vigueur à titre provisoire, plusieurs pays de l'UE ne l'ont ainsi toujours pas ratifié.

item.title: Saudi pipeline outage threatens loss of 4% of global oil supply
item.description: Saudi Arabia will run out of oil stocks for exports if it doesn't restart its major pipeline to the Red Sea within days, Saudi oil buyers and traders said.
item.dc:creator: Alex Lawler, Dmitry Zhdannikov
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia will run out of oil stocks for exports if it doesn't restart its major pipeline to the Red Sea within days, leading to a loss of up to 4% of global supply, Saudi oil buyers and traders said. A further decline in Saudi flows will worsen the global supply crunch, which has already pushed global fuel prices to record highs, spurred inflation around the world and sent U.S. bond yields to the highest levels since the 2008 financial crisis. Since drone attacks forced Saudi Arabia to [USN:S8N44107L TEXT:"shut"] its huge east-west oil pipeline on Friday, Riyadh has not given full details about the extent of the damage or how long the route will stay off-line. Sources that spoke to Reuters gave varying estimates, with one saying the damage could take as long as five to six weeks to repair, while another said it could be fixed sooner and could resume pumping partially while repairs are ongoing. Saudi Arabia's government media office and energy ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment. For the past six months, the pipeline running through the desert across the Arabian Peninsula has spared Saudi Arabia from the brunt of the impact of the wartime shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz that has crippled exports from its neighbours. The world's biggest exporter has used the pipeline to reroute around 4 million barrels per day — around 4% of global supply — to the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea. But with the pipeline out of service, Yanbu now has stocks to maintain exports for just five to seven days, according to three industry sources familiar with Saudi exports. Saudi Arabia also has stocks to supply customers for several days from Egypt's ports of Ain Sukhna on the Red Sea and Sidi Kerir on the Mediterranean, a fourth source said. Yanbu storage capacity stands at around 35 million barrels, according to industry estimates, with Ain Sukhna and Sidi Kerir able to store 18 million and 20 million barrels respectively. Stocks are not full and will ultimately run out without the east-west pipeline resuming operations, the four sources said. Saudi oil supply has already fallen to a more than [USN:L6N4530LR TEXT:"three-decade low"] in August on reduced flows via Hormuz and the Red Sea, the International Energy Agency said on Friday. World oil supply will [USN:L6N4530I5 TEXT:"decline"] this year by 5.7 million bpd, or about 6%, the IEA, which coordinates Western energy policies, said.In addition to the attack on the pipeline, Houthi fighters in Yemen who have threatened Saudi oil shipments seized an island on Friday in the mouth of the Red Sea . The Middle East supplied around 22 million barrels per day of oil before the war. Flows through the Strait of Hormuz have slowed to just 6 million to 9 million bpd, industry sources say. Saudi Arabia told OPEC last week that its oil production had dropped to just 6.2 million bpd in August from 10.9 million bpd in February before the start of the war.

item.title: Carney pushes idea of making Canada 'associate member' of EU, WSJ reports
item.description: The EU is open to the idea, the Journal reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney wants a closer relationship with the European Union and is exploring whether his country could become an "associate member" of the bloc, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday. The EU, which has not been flexible about membership rules in the past, is open to the idea of granting Canada a yet-to-be-created status of associate membership, the newspaper reported, citing unnamed officials both from the EU and Canada. Canada's embassy in Brussels and spokespeople at the European Commission did not respond to separate requests for comment. Canada's [USN:L6N4500OF TEXT:"escalating trade war"] with the United States has added urgency to its strategic pivot towards other trading partners. Relations between Ottawa and Washington have deteriorated sharply since President Donald Trump returned to the White House last year due to disagreements over trade and other issues. The trade dispute has led to tariffs on tens of billions of dollars in cross-border trade. Canada and the EU are discussing ways of allowing Canada's goods, services and workers involved in strategic supply chains such as energy, AI, defence and critical minerals to move freely, thus effectively shifting the EU border, the Wall Street Journal said. Canada and the EU are also talking about laying underwater cables, jointly constructing data centres, cloud storage and new satellite networks as well as infrastructure to ship Canadian energy to the EU, the newspaper said. Carney has spoken regularly with several EU leaders, most notably French President Emmanuel Macron, about the possibility of letting Canadians live and work visa-free in the EU, the WSJ said, citing two unnamed officials familiar with the matter. Macron's press office did not respond to a request for comment. Macron's office separately confirmed that he will meet Carney on September 20 in the French territory of Saint Pierre and Miquelon, a group of islands off Canada's Atlantic coast. The meeting marks the first official visit by a Canadian prime minister to the archipelago and "symbolises the strength of the relationship that unites our two countries," the Elysee said. Any project to forge closer ties between Canada and the EU likely faces challenges, however, based on past efforts to implement a more modest trade deal, which has faced fierce opposition within Europe. More than a decade after the deal was struck and nine years since it provisionally entered into force, several EU countries still have not ratified it.

item.title: Lithuania says drone sighting turns out to be flock of birds, after NATO summons jets
item.description: Authorities closed Vilnius airport and NATO summoned at least one fighter jet.
item.dc:creator: Andrius Sytas
item.content:encoded: Lithuania said that a perceived drone sighting in its airspace earlier on Sunday that prompted authorities to close Vilnius airport and NATO to summon at least one fighter jet, turned out to be a flock of birds. The air alert was lifted and the airport reopened within 38 minutes, after the NATO jet made a visual identification, Lithuania's National Crisis Management Centre said. "On initial radar readings, marks left by birds and drones can be similar," it added in a statement. A jet had been summoned from Siauliai in northern Lithuania, the centre said, where the Italian air force is currently based as part of the NATO Baltic Air Defence mission. [USN:L8N41X1AC TEXT:"Military drones straying"] into the airspace of Finland, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania are stoking concerns that the war in Ukraine is spilling over into NATO's northern borders with Russia. The Vilnius marathon, which was taking place in the capital, was not interrupted, the organisers told Reuters.

item.title: GE HealthCare in talks over possible $1 billion deal for Sofie Biosciences, FT reports
item.description: GE HealthCare Technologies is in talks over a possible $1 billion deal to buy radiopharmaceutical developer Sofie Biosciences, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: GE HealthCare Technologies (GEHC.O) is in talks over a possible $1 billion deal to buy radiopharmaceutical developer Sofie Biosciences, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter. Here are some details: A deal for Sofie, which specializes in radioactive chemicals used in cancer scans, could be announced as soon as next week, the report said. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. GE HealthCare declined to comment while Sofie Biosciences could not be immediately reached for comment outside regular business hours. The potential deal would be GE HealthCare’s second major acquisition since it broke away as part of U.S. conglomerate General Electric’s (GE.N) three-way split in 2024. Acquiring Sofie would help bolster GE HealthCare’s pharmaceutical diagnostics division, which supplies the agents and chemicals used in scans, the report said.

item.title: Russia hits passenger train on Ukraine's border with Poland, just misses 'diplomatic train'
